content:
Solar panel insurance should identify the complete photovoltaic installation, its owner and the project stage. A policy mentioning the building does not by itself establish protection for panels, an inverter or electricity income. For a Moldovan business preparing its 2027 budget, the useful starting point is a component inventory linked to actual replacement costs.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Who should review the installation?

The discussion is relevant to factories using rooftop solar, farms powering sorting or irrigation, commercial-property owners and electricity producers. A tenant, building owner and equipment financier may have different interests. Record who owns each part and who bears repair costs under the installation, lease and financing documents.

Separate operating equipment from modules awaiting installation. Include supporting structures, cabling, controls and protective equipment where relevant. Identify batteries as a separate system, rather than assuming that the expression solar panels includes energy storage. Review the configuration using the BESS equipment and operational-risk guide.

As one local category observation, DONARIS VIG's property page lists photovoltaic parks. Checked on 25 November 2026, this does not confirm rooftop acceptance, batteries, interruption, tariffs or placement through ING Broker.

Risks and exclusions to compare

Ask for specific answers about hail, wind, fire, theft, electrical damage and accidental inverter breakdown. These are questions for the proposed policy, not a declaration that every installation receives these protections. The insurer's event definitions and equipment list matter more than an all-risks label.

Check how the proposed conditions treat wear, known defects, faulty installation, warranty obligations and gradual loss of efficiency. Ask whether access equipment, dismantling, transport and reinstallation have separate limits. An expense necessary to restore production is not automatically payable under insurance.

What should change in the 2027 planning file?

The Ministry of Energy's communication of 20 August 2026 describes simplified installation procedures. Checked on 25 November 2026, it is policy context, not permission for this project or an insurance condition. This supports checking how newly added equipment changes the 2027 insurance inventory; it does not predict insurance demand. Administrative simplification does not certify an installation's safety or add cover. Retain the technical and commissioning records applicable to your actual project.

Use a planning scenario, not a weather or revenue forecast: an inverter fails while roof panels remain intact. Identify the correct replacement model, supplier lead time, access arrangements and the business activity affected. Compare a confirmed spare-part response with assumptions, and update the file when equipment is added during 2027.

Prevention before the next operating period

Ask competent specialists to review fixing arrangements, visible damage and outstanding service recommendations against the installation records. Keep monitoring alerts linked to actual inspections and repairs. Do not treat a cleared software notification as proof that a physical defect was removed, and do not climb onto the roof to complete an insurance questionnaire.

Price: compare the same system

No verified 2027 premium is available for your installation in this guide. An individual calculation needs values, configuration, site, operating stage, maintenance and requested protections. The premium is the price of insurance; the deductible is the part of a loss retained by the insured under the contract. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

Ask for comparable proposals using the same inventory and valuation basis. Keep property repair separate from the assessment of business interruption and financial consequences. Reduced sunlight, a change in electricity prices and a component damaged by an accepted event are different situations; do not budget an insurance payment for all three.

Documents for assessment

Prepare the owner and site details, equipment inventory, invoices or replacement estimates, installation and acceptance documents, maintenance history and known defects. Add a description of self-consumption or electricity sales if interruption consequences are being discussed. Share sensitive technical plans only through an agreed channel.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The DONARIS property page, rechecked on 26 November 2026, lists photovoltaic parks. This verifies a local category, not acceptance of this rooftop, a battery, lost income or ING placement.

  • Existing rooftop: compare panels and inverter with the roof and building. Prepare the component inventory, ownership and supported values. Check which items and address are actually named; a building entry is not a substitute for the equipment list.
  • Delivery or installation: compare transport, works, testing and handover separately. Prepare the programme and acceptance records. Check the accepted stage and transition date instead of assuming an operating-property response also applies during installation.
  • Storage or capacity added in 2027: compare the new equipment and dependencies with the previous configuration. Prepare the new description and values. Request separate confirmation for batteries and financial consequences; investment approval does not amend insurance.

Frequently asked questions

What determines the price of solar panel insurance?

Present the installation value, roof or ground location, components, stage and requested risks. Ask whether the calculation includes the inverter, access and reinstallation. Compare the same inventory, limits and deductible; a cheaper panel-only proposal is not equivalent to a broader system assessment. No fixed 2027 rate is confirmed here.

Which documents should a company prepare first?

Start with ownership or use documents, the component inventory, invoices or replacement estimates, installation and acceptance records, warranties and service history. Identify batteries separately. Mark missing records and known defects rather than describing the file as complete. The insurer may request further documents for the actual project.

What should we do after hail or an observed inverter fault?

Prioritize safety and competent technical assistance. Record the observation time and available monitoring information without climbing onto a roof or opening electrical equipment. Follow the actual policy notification procedure and request instructions about inspection, evidence and repairs. Neither the observed damage nor a repair invoice alone establishes acceptance of a claim.

Does an installer warranty replace an insurance assessment?

Read the supplier warranty and the proposed policy as separate documents. Ask who must respond to a defect, which expenses each document addresses and how any exclusions interact. A warranty claim does not establish an insurance payment, while insurance is not a promise that the installer will fulfil every contractual duty.

Are batteries and lost electricity income included with the panels?

Do not assume one answer covers all three. Identify the BESS configuration separately and describe self-consumption or electricity sales if interruption is being assessed. The proposal must explain accepted events, equipment, calculation basis and limits. Reduced sunlight or a lower electricity price is not automatically the same event as insured physical damage.

Discuss the installation with ING Broker. Insurance ING Broker SRL acts as broker, not as the insurer paying claims. Availability, acceptance, exclusions and compensation depend on the actual insurer's contract.
